The two baseline reds are attributed by the run's own arm-control run (arm-control.log) to the git-archive measurement tree rather than to the revision -- the same two ids fail against a head-revision extraction -- so their absence at head is a tree artefact, not a silent fix; the attribution reproduces and is sound.

findings.text: the new rule ok = exit_status is not None also flips a replay that never ran -- no stored command, a prose command, an unresolved integrated revision, a checkout that does not descend from it -- from ok true to ok false, a wider behaviour change than the timeout case; no test in the population asserts the refusal paths' ok value, and the plan's done-when names only the timeout and no-status cases. The node documents this in the fragment, so it is reported rather than triaged.

the section records the measured payload as carrying finding null; at the node's base revision 9443e674a a timed-out replay already produced a finding naming the bound (the base payload inside negative-control.log shows it), so that half of the reproduction does not hold. The node reports this explicitly in its fragment rather than assuming it; the plan owner should correct the section's reproduction statement.

justifications.durability: tests/test_a_timed_out_replay_is_not_ok.py pins all four behaviours and isolates itself in a temporary RECKON_HOME while asserting the real run directory gained nothing; the declared mutation (base promotion.py with the head test) reddens the timeout case and the recorded payload shows ok true beside exit_status None, so the guard is shown to fire rather than merely not to. The ok rule is stated as one line whose comment explains the semantics (a status was measured, not that the gate passed).
justifications.evidence: every arm is captured with a header naming the revision, the tree, the literal command, the measurement cwd and the module as imported, each ending on a bare EXIT= line; the base and head arms, the arm-control attribution of the two base reds, the negative control and the named gate are all in the run directory, and I re-ran the named gate (4 passed in 64.68s, EXIT=0) and the negative control (1 failed in 23.30s, EXIT=1, ok true beside exit_status None) myself. Held below full because the arms are not at tree parity -- base measured in a git-archive extraction, head in the worktree -- which is precisely why the two base reds needed the arm-control run.
justifications.fit: commit subjects are conventional with bodies that state what changed and why, carry no AI attribution and no plan or ticket identifier; the source and test name the mechanism (_replay_cut_short_reason, cut_short, replay_elapsed_seconds) with no section label in code, and the pre-existing ruff findings in promotion.py are unchanged by this commit.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the defect opens on a field a caller reads first: with no ok key in the result the CLI's {'ok': True, **result} merge published ok true beside a null exit status, and the replay log stopped after three header lines. Both are repaired at the source -- report['ok'] is false whenever no exit status was produced, and the log carries a '# cut short:' sentence naming the bound, its source and the seconds elapsed -- and the router through record_gate_rerun_at_integrated_revision honours the field the CLI already merges, so no CLI change is needed. Held below full by the broader refusal-path flip, which is correct but extends beyond the stated defect.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff 9443e674a..f8f7d24eb shows exactly reckon/crew/promotion.py (+95/-12), tests/test_a_timed_out_replay_is_not_ok.py (new, 277 lines) and docs/evidence/fragments/crew-runtime-positive-controls/a-timed-out-replay-is-not-ok.html (+53 and two one-line corrections), all declared write paths, with no unrelated edits and no shared-index or plan-state mutation.
